# Quantum Learning Anisotropy

This project studies label-dependent local gradient energies in an interacting,
particle-number-conserving quantum random circuit. Conserved-density labels
have a polynomial ensemble energy floor at diffusive depth. Complementary
phase labels have an exponentially small full native gradient. The tasks share
an average input state, circuit, readout, and efficient encoder.

## Story and exact-result route

- README.md — Question, central comparison, reading routes, and scope.
- science/model.md — Authoritative circuit ensemble, input source, operational
  loss, native tangent basis, full-gradient theorems, and quantifiers.
- science/data_encoding.md — Dual-rail encoder, extensive nuisance family,
  same high-rank average state, exact decoder, and native resource costs.
- science/coherence_bound.md — Fixed-schedule exclusion process, imported
  negative-dependence theorems, charge concentration, interference second
  moment, and all-coordinate Parseval/Haar argument.
- science/density_transport.md — Population contrast, Fourier-mode estimates,
  marked Haar block, first-layer lower bound, and general-profile extension.
- science/loss_and_geometry.md — Exact axial gradient covariance, operational
  loss versus other losses, probability consequences, and shot resources.
- science/interpretation.md — Physical synthesis and consequences permitted
  by the bounds.
- science/finite_size.md — Stable evaluation of the explicit analytic bounds
  and the practical limits of their constants.
- references/RELATED_WORK.md — Attribution and theorem-level comparison.
- references/references.bib — Structured bibliographic records.
- verification/README.md — Commands, expected assertions, and verification
  scope.

## Essential distinctions

The observable is fixed physical Z_0. The expected error is that of a random
prediction drawn from its measurement. The density lower is for the square
of the population-loss gradient, not the average of per-example squares.
The phase bound is an actual squared-amplitude and full-gradient estimate;
a zero first moment would not establish it.

The native metric is the sum over six specified norm-one left tangents per
local gate. The identity derivative vanishes but is retained in M=3nD.
Coordinate independence is not assumed.

Concentration is conditioned on both the matching schedule and the nuisance
input. Mixtures of strongly Rayleigh measures are not assumed strongly
Rayleigh. Averaging is performed after the valid bounds.

The logical tasks share the same average density operator, not the same
supplied pure-state ensemble. A common inverse encoder works for all nuisance
values; different logical axes use their appropriate final basis rotation.

The polynomial density moment does not establish typical trainability or
convergence. The exponential phase upper controls typical local gradients,
but does not prohibit all learning strategies. The explicit decoder rules
out a data-hardness interpretation. The data's nuisance entropy does not
certify noise robustness.

## Reproduction

Run python3 verification/run_all.py from the repository root.
Finite checks use the written tolerances; they do not prove asymptotic
scaling or literature novelty.
